day: Saturday of week 23 in Ordinary Time or The Most Holy Name of Mary or Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
text:
There is a deep consistency running through what we hear today. Paul speaks about communion—real, binding communion with Christ in the Eucharist, not a casual symbol but a true sharing that shapes who we are. Jesus then teaches about fruit: that we become known by what we produce, that our words and actions flow from what we actually treasure in our hearts. The two readings are saying something similar. You cannot live in communion with Christ and live otherwise. You cannot drink from his cup and pretend it doesn't change you.

This is not about perfection or never stumbling. It is about direction, about where our deepest loyalty lies. When we come to this table, we are not simply receiving something. We are being drawn into communion with the body of Christ, which means we are committing ourselves to a way of living that comes from that bond. The good tree produces good fruit not through effort alone, but because its roots draw nourishment from good soil. Our roots, Paul reminds us, are in Christ.

Perhaps today you might simply notice: what am I building my life on? Where do I actually go for strength and belonging? Is there some small way I can deepen my communion with Christ, to let that shape what I say and do?
